rubrics.justification: The response largely restates the provided Gardner 3AA label rather than the actual image. The image does not clearly show a classic well-expanded Day 5 3AA blastocyst with a tightly defined ICM and cohesive TE; those features are overstated from the visible morphology.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, BMI, prior cycle outcome, sperm parameters, and embryo grade into prognosis reasonably well, though some inferences about the DOR discrepancy are speculative.

The reasoning is structured and mostly internally consistent, with a clear link from embryo grade and age to prognosis. Minor issues include overconfidence in morphology and some speculative deductions about ovarian response and implantation factors.

Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based (SET, luteal support, reassessing uterine factors after failure), but recommending ERA after only one prior failed cycle and suggesting immunologic/NK-cell testing are not strongly guideline-supported.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, endometrial assessment, and follow-up investigations if failure recurs. Some recommendations are useful but a few are more aggressive than typical first-line practice.
